output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: resolveServletInternal only normalized the path (ResourceUtil.normalize) and checked isPathAllowed. Neither collapses nor rejects segments with 3+ consecutive dots, so a path-traversal segment like "..." reaches the resource lookup and can resolve an attacker-controlled servlet resource.

Fix (mirrors upstream commit b54d4e6693e0): added package-private static SlingServletResolver.isInvalidPath(String) that scans each '/'-delimited segment and returns true when any segment consists of more than two consecutive dots. resolveServletInternal now returns null immediately when isInvalidPath(scriptNameOrResourceType) is true, before any normalization or resource lookup. This guards all three entry points (resolveServlet by request, resolveServlet(resource, scriptName), and resolveServlet(resolver, scriptName)) since they all funnel through resolveServletInternal.

Behavior preserved: single-dot ("./") and double-dot ("../") segments and dots embedded within a segment (e.g. foo.bar.baz.servlet) are unaffected — only 3+ consecutive-dot segments are rejected. null/empty input is treated as not-invalid so existing callers behave unchanged.

Verification: POV (PovCve202423673Test) went from exit 0 (vulnerable, servlet resolved) before the patch to exit 1 (assertion fails, resolveServlet returns null) after. Added SlingServletResolverInvalidPathTest (7 cases) passes. Full clean suite: 172 tests, 0 failures.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change adds a guard that only rejects paths containing segments of 3+ consecutive dots, which are never valid Sling resource paths. Legitimate resource types, absolute script paths, and normal relative/dot segments are unaffected. The new logic runs once per resolution with negligible cost. One caveat: if any deployment intentionally registered a servlet at a path literally containing a "..."-style segment, it would no longer resolve — but such a path is not a valid/normalizable Sling path and matches upstream's intended behavior. Note: running the POV via `mvn test` leaves a stale compiled class in target/test-classes; always use `mvn clean test` (or -Dtest scoping) to avoid a false failure from the removed POV source.
output_json.summary: Fixed CVE-2024-23673 / SLING-12233 (CWE-022 path traversal) in Apache Sling Servlets Resolver by rejecting resource-type/script paths that contain an invalid path segment (a segment of more than two consecutive dots, e.g. "..."). Such segments are not collapsed by ResourceUtil.normalize nor blocked by isPathAllowed, so an attacker-registered servlet under a "/libs/proxy/.../uploaded.servlet"-style path was resolved and executed. Added a static isInvalidPath(String) helper to SlingServletResolver and an early return at the top of resolveServletInternal so that any request/resolution using such a path returns null before resource lookup.
